messages.author: 72117544927b4912
messages.subject: Mrds abundance estimation in R
parts:
Hello, 

I am working on small cetacean data with a double platform (acoustic/visual) conducted in line-transect distance sampling framework. Each detection is composed of a group of individuals. I therefore have information on the groupsize for each detection. 
From this, I fitted a detection function with point independence configuration. 

To estimate abundance,  I used the Horvitz-Thompson-like estimator (dht function) and the output was for individuals only. I guess the abundance estimate was not correct, how can I get the abundance estimate for clusters? Need I add something in my code? 

pi.abund <- dht(model=pi.mr.dist.swell.hn,
                region=tables$region.table,
                sample=tables$sample.table, obs=tables$obs.table,
                se=TRUE,options=list(convert.units=0.001))


I hope I am clear and you can understand my problem. I've been struggling for hours without coming to a conclusion. Any help would be very welcome :)

Thank you!
Camille

Have you named the group size column in your data "size".
If your data have a column named "size" then the abundance / density of both individuals and cluster should be output. If you have done this and it is still not working then please send your data and code across and I will take a look.

Best wishes,

Laura

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Mrds abundance estimation in R
parts:
Camille

Looking at the help file for dht​ I see the object produced by dht​ (`pi.abund`) in your case, is a list consisting of three objects:

clusters    
result list for object clusters

individuals 
result list for individuals

Expected.S  
data.frame of estimates of expected cluster size with fields Region, Expected.S and se.Expected.S If each cluster size=1, then the result only includes individuals and not clusters and Expected.S.

Hence, I expect you should be able to
print(pi.abund$clusters)

to get information about abundance or density of clusters.

Here is an example from the "tee data"; not using point independence:

data(book.tee.data)
region <- book.tee.data$book.tee.region
egdata <- book.tee.data$book.tee.dataframe
samples <- book.tee.data$book.tee.samples
obs <- book.tee.data$book.tee.obs
result <- ddf(dsmodel = ~mcds(key = "hn", formula = ~1),
              data = egdata[egdata$observer==1, ], method = "ds",
              meta.data = list(width = 4))
out <- dht(result,region,samples,obs,options=list(varflag=0,group=TRUE),
          se=TRUE)
print(out$clusters$N)

I divided the transects into segments to estimate ESW based on environmental conditions.
To estimate abundance, I first considered the length of the segment as Effort, but I realized that the model did not consider the total length of the segments for each block, but only considered the segments where there were detections. I think I was incorrect.

I would like to confirm with you that the Effort should be the total length of the surveyed transects for each block? (which means I will get 130km instead of 14km for the block 8b?)




When I add up all the ON EFFORT segments of block 8b, I have about 130 km of segments.



Thank you for your help,
Best regards

Camille Ollier

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Mrds abundance estimation in R
parts:
Camille

Given your experience that the effort calculations did not appear correct using the approach you describe, I think you will need to construct the region, sample and obs tables manually.

I refer you to the dht​ documentation that describes the contents of these three tables:

region.table      
data.frame of region records. Two columns: Region.Label and Area. If only density is required, one can set Area=0 for all regions.

sample.table      
data.frame of sample records. Three columns: Region.Label, Sample.Label, Effort.

obs.table   
data.frame of observation records with fields: object, Region.Label, and Sample.Label which give links to sample.table, region.table and the data records used in model. Not necessary if the data.frame used to create the model contains Region.Label, Sample.Label columns.

region.table contains only two columns: the names of the strata (blocks in your case?) and their sizes. sample.table is most critical in your situation because that is where Effort is defined, namely the length of each transect. sample.table has three columns, the transect names and their lengths and the strata to which those transects belong.

As you can see from the description, the obs.table is unnecessary if your mrds_table​ data frame contains Region.Label and Sample.Label fields.
